{"findings": [

    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Potential TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or undefined",
    "body": "`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and can be `undefined` when the array is empty or when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null. The condition then dereferences it with `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== \"google_calendar\"` without optional chaining. When an event with Google Meet location has no destination calendar, this throws and aborts the booking flow. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== \"google_calendar\"` or explicitly guard for undefined."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/core/EventManager.ts",
    "line": 554,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Reschedule cleanup only removes first old calendar event",
    "body": "In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `newBookingId` is set for a reschedule and old events need to be removed, the old calendar event is selected with `booking.references.find(...)`. Since this PR now supports multiple calendar references, only the first old calendar event is deleted; events for other hosts remain on their calendars, causing stale or duplicate events after reschedule. Filter all old calendar references and delete each."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts",
    "line": 454,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Recurring cancellation only cancels first calendar reference per booking",
    "body": "In the recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch, each updated booking's calendar reference is selected with `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes(\"_calendar\"))`. With multiple calendar references now possible, this cancels only one calendar event per recurring instance and silently leaves other hosts' calendar events intact. All calendar references for each updated booking should be iterated and scheduled for deletion."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts",
    "line": 1074,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Collective team destination calendars not added when organizer has none",
    "body": "`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. Then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so for collective events where only team members have destination calendars, those calendars are never added and no events are created for them. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array before pushing, for example `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/types/Calendar.d.ts",
    "line": 221,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "Calendar.createEvent contract changed without updating all implementations",
    "body": "The `Calendar` interface now requires `credentialId` in `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. However LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and BaseCalendarService still implement `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with only one parameter. This is a contract break that will cause TypeScript errors and a build failure. Update all implementations to accept and use the credentialId, or make the interface parameter optional."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 255,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Fallback calendar selection condition is impossible",
    "body": "In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is truthy, the else branch never runs; if it is falsy, the predicate compares against a falsy value and never matches, leaving `selectedCalendar` undefined. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` around line 317. Updating or deleting events with a null/undefined `externalCalendarId` will target an undefined calendarId and fail. Use a fallback that selects the appropriate destination (e.g., first destination or by credential)."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 122,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Organizer email uses first destination calendar for all created events",
    "body": "In `createEvent` and `updateEvent`, the organizer attendee email is set to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`, where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first item of `destinationCalendar`. When multiple collective hosts each have their own destination calendar, events created for later credentials still use the first host's calendar externalId as organizer email, resulting in incorrect organizer identity and potentially invalid IDs. The destination matching the credential being used should determine the organizer email."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts",
    "line": 151,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Reversed slug/requestedSlug conditions for organization creation",
    "body": "The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. This reverses the intended behavior: now when team billing is enabled, both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set, and when disabled, neither is set. This likely breaks organization slug assignment for non-billing deployments. Restore the original conditions."
  },
  {
    "file": "packages/lib/CalendarService.ts",
    "line": 156,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "CalDAV createEvent ignores credentialId and uses only first destination",
    "body": "`BaseCalendarService.createEvent` does not accept the new `credentialId` parameter and always uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (the first entry in `event.destinationCalendar`) to select the calendar. In multi-host collective events, every credential will create the event on the same first host's CalDAV calendar, causing duplicates on one calendar and missing events on the others. It must select the destination calendar matching the credential being used."
  }

findings.title: Potential TypeError when destinationCalendar is empty or undefined
findings.body: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and can be `undefined` when the array is empty or when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null. The condition then dereferences it with `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. When an event with Google Meet location has no destination calendar, this throws and aborts the booking flow. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` or explicitly guard for undefined.

findings.title: Reschedule cleanup only removes first old calendar event
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, when `newBookingId` is set for a reschedule and old events need to be removed, the old calendar event is selected with `booking.references.find(...)`. Since this PR now supports multiple calendar references, only the first old calendar event is deleted; events for other hosts remain on their calendars, causing stale or duplicate events after reschedule. Filter all old calendar references and delete each.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation only cancels first calendar reference per booking
findings.body: In the recurring `allRemainingBookings` branch, each updated booking's calendar reference is selected with `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`. With multiple calendar references now possible, this cancels only one calendar event per recurring instance and silently leaves other hosts' calendar events intact. All calendar references for each updated booking should be iterated and scheduled for deletion.

findings.title: Collective team destination calendars not added when organizer has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists. Then `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op on `null`, so for collective events where only team members have destination calendars, those calendars are never added and no events are created for them. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array before pushing, for example `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: Calendar.createEvent contract changed without updating all implementations
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface now requires `credentialId` in `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`. However LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and BaseCalendarService still implement `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` with only one parameter. This is a contract break that will cause TypeScript errors and a build failure. Update all implementations to accept and use the credentialId, or make the interface parameter optional.

findings.title: Fallback calendar selection condition is impossible
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. If `externalCalendarId` is truthy, the else branch never runs; if it is falsy, the predicate compares against a falsy value and never matches, leaving `selectedCalendar` undefined. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` around line 317. Updating or deleting events with a null/undefined `externalCalendarId` will target an undefined calendarId and fail. Use a fallback that selects the appropriate destination (e.g., first destination or by credential).

findings.title: Organizer email uses first destination calendar for all created events
findings.body: In `createEvent` and `updateEvent`, the organizer attendee email is set to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`, where `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first item of `destinationCalendar`. When multiple collective hosts each have their own destination calendar, events created for later credentials still use the first host's calendar externalId as organizer email, resulting in incorrect organizer identity and potentially invalid IDs. The destination matching the credential being used should determine the organizer email.

findings.title: Reversed slug/requestedSlug conditions for organization creation
findings.body: The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`. This reverses the intended behavior: now when team billing is enabled, both `slug` and `requestedSlug` are set, and when disabled, neither is set. This likely breaks organization slug assignment for non-billing deployments. Restore the original conditions.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent ignores credentialId and uses only first destination
findings.body: `BaseCalendarService.createEvent` does not accept the new `credentialId` parameter and always uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar` (the first entry in `event.destinationCalendar`) to select the calendar. In multi-host collective events, every credential will create the event on the same first host's CalDAV calendar, causing duplicates on one calendar and missing events on the others. It must select the destination calendar matching the credential being used.
